programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Alistair Appleton helps a young couple search for their first home together in the Oxfordshire countryside. They are hoping for space to accommodate a rabbit palace and an impressive collection of houseplants. Alistair also pays a visit to the University of Oxford Botanic Garden, where he discovers how nature is inspiring exciting new technological developments.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo and Joe are in Stockport to help Sasha and Rick transform their long, muddy, unloved garden into a wild English wonderland. With unsafe concrete steps making the patio hard to access, it’s no place for daughter Jocelyn or the new baby on the way, and hosting friends and family is a real challenge. The couple dream of a vibrant, wildlife-friendly space, bursting with colourful flowers and plants, where their children can grow up with adventure and magic all around. They want a practical design too, with a clear divide between patio and grass so that their rescue dog Nelly can roam without tracking mud indoors. Having spent the last 18 months renovating their home while raising Jocelyn and preparing for their second child, Sasha and Rick are ready for their garden to finally match their family’s energy and joy. Can the team deliver their dream sanctuary on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four take on the Bridge of Lies. In this episode, it's family and friends Lynne, Derek, John and Kenny. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo and Joe are in Stockport to help Sasha and Rick transform their long, muddy, unloved garden into a wild English wonderland. programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four take on the Bridge of Lies. In this episode, it's family and friends Lynne, Derek, John and Kenny. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

With unsafe concrete steps making the patio hard to access, it’s no place for daughter Jocelyn or the new baby on the way, and hosting friends and family is a real challenge. The couple dream of a vibrant, wildlife-friendly space, bursting with colourful flowers and plants, where their children can grow up with adventure and magic all around. They want a practical design too, with a clear divide between patio and grass so that their rescue dog Nelly can roam without tracking mud indoors. Having spent the last 18 months renovating their home while raising Jocelyn and preparing for their second child, Sasha and Rick are ready for their garden to finally match their family’s energy and joy. Can the team deliver their dream sanctuary on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four take on the Bridge of Lies. In this episode, it's family and friends Lynne, Derek, John and Kenny. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc: Flo and Joe are in Stockport to help Sasha and Rick transform their long, muddy, unloved garden into a wild English wonderland. With unsafe concrete steps making the patio hard to access, it’s no place for daughter Jocelyn or the new baby on the way, and hosting friends and family is a real challenge. The couple dream of a vibrant, wildlife-friendly space, bursting with colourful flowers and plants, where their children can grow up with adventure and magic all around. They want a practical design too, with a clear divide between patio and grass so that their rescue dog Nelly can roam without tracking mud indoors. Having spent the last 18 months renovating their home while raising Jocelyn and preparing for their second child, Sasha and Rick are ready for their garden to finally match their family’s energy and joy. Can the team deliver their dream sanctuary on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four take on the Bridge of Lies. In this episode, it's family and friends Lynne, Derek, John and Kenny. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

With unsafe concrete steps making the patio hard to access, it’s no place for daughter Jocelyn or the new baby on the way, and hosting friends and family is a real challenge. The couple dream of a vibrant, wildlife-friendly space, bursting with colourful flowers and plants, where their children can grow up with adventure and magic all around. They want a practical design too, with a clear divide between patio and grass so that their rescue dog Nelly can roam without tracking mud indoors. Having spent the last 18 months renovating their home while raising Jocelyn and preparing for their second child, Sasha and Rick are ready for their garden to finally match their family’s energy and joy. Can the team deliver their dream sanctuary on a £4,000 budget?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four take on the Bridge of Lies. In this episode, it's family and friends Lynne, Derek, John and Kenny. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Banjo and Ro’s Grand Island Hotel
programme.desc: Interior designer Banjo and his husband Ro tackle the vast ruined entrance of Ulva House – can they transform it into a breathtaking lobby worthy of their Hebridean dream?

programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Jo and Andy must take stock of the rain damage to their wheat crop. A huge chasm has torn through one field and in another the seedlings are swamped in mud. They call in a grain specialist for some expert advice. Meanwhile one of their pedigree cattle goes into labour. It's touch and go as Andy helps deliver a calf that's in breech position. Near Glasgow, John and Antoinette run a mixed livestock farm, but John badly needs a hip replacement and is struggling with the workload. Their youngest son Ben wants to help, but the farm can't afford to pay him full-time. Their six kids have come up with a plan to boost the farm's income by setting up an events business. In Caithness, single mum Sally Crowe runs a croft with help from her 79-year-old dad Iain. It's one of the biggest days of the year, as they find out how many lambs to expect in spring on a small farm where every penny counts.

programme.title: Reported Missing
programme.desc: Police concerns grow about the mental state of two missing teens - 16-year-old Larissa has disappeared after an argument with her mum, and 18-year-old Bobby may be a suicide risk.

programme.title: Disaster at Sea: The Piper Alpha Story
programme.desc: Piper Alpha burns, and the platform begins to collapse. With 167 men dead and just a handful of survivors, grief turns to fury, and the fight for justice begins back home.

programme.title: Scotcast
programme.desc: Conversation about Scotland’s biggest news stories, hosted by Martin Geissler.

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: An oddball family make a brave, but bungling, attempt to save their failing funeral home in the sleepy Scottish fishing village of Kincully. Archie, having recently inherited the floundering family business from his domineering dad, is determined to prove himself. His sister Moira, the company mortician, and hearse driver Cousin Ron are looking to Archie to prevent A Better Place Funeral Home from falling into the hands of Sympathy Plus, a corporate funeral chain run by the power-hungry Eileen. Archie is also living in the shadow of his late father - literally. He keeps him in a great big freezer on the landing. With time running out, Archie hatches a plan to keep hold of the family business. Will Archie’s scheme work? Or will A Better Place fall prey to Eileen’s growing empire?

programme.title: BBC Comedy Short Films
programme.desc: Calamity James is a slapstick comedy about a young man, James, who is cursed with ‘acute misfortune syndrome’. James tries to reconnect with his dad after being thrown out by his mum for setting fire to their house at a family barbecue. In this world, chronic bad luck exists and the unbelievable is the everyday.

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy’s recovery is back on track after he and John put his hand to the test. The pair are training again, and the search for Tommy’s next opponent begins. Eager to make the most of family time, Tommy splashes out on a £90,000 motor home for family trips with Molly and Bambi and takes his mum out for lunch and a long-overdue catch-up. Tommy reveals that John has had a recent health scare, so to cheer him up, father and son take their very different caravans to a local steam fair. It’s vital for Tommy’s mental health that he keeps physically active at all times, so he sets his sights on an ambitious new goal - a 100km triathlon. Meanwhile, John worries that the physical toll from this could jeopardise the chances of Tommy recovering and landing a big money fight. As Tommy throws himself into training for the triathlon, one question remains - can he avoid getting injured, or will this new challenge end his boxing career for good?

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy realises just how far he and Molly have come since their separation last year, but John’s worries grow as Tommy takes on a 100km triathlon, pushing his body to new physical limits. Before the challenge, Tommy takes some downtime at the spa with his mates, preparing for a huge press push ahead of his series premiere. He’s come a long way since he and Molly separated last year, and the truth hits home when he sees his face on a billboard - and shares the moment with Molly. The premiere brings together family and friends, all celebrating how far Tommy has come. But there’s no time to rest - he heads to the south of France for the triathlon, where Molly and Bambi surprise him at the finishing line. Even with the triathlon behind him, Tommy’s pursuit of physical challenges continues as he gears up for the Great North Run the following week. Riding a high, he is suddenly hit with a backlash on social media, leaving him to wonder what he can do to catch a break.

programme.title: Tommy: The Good. The Bad. The Fury
programme.desc: Tommy’s childhood friend Chris asks him to do a book reading at the school where they once studied. Tommy faces his nerves and steps up, inspiring students to dream big and believe anything is possible. Tragedy then strikes with the passing of boxing legend Ricky Hatton - a devastating loss for his friends, family and Manchester. Tommy trained with Ricky for 18 months, and his friend and mentor’s passing reminds him how important it is to live life to the fullest. Tommy sets out on the most gruelling test of endurance possible: climbing the three highest mountains in England, Scotland and Wales in just 24 hours. Battling brutal conditions and exhaustion, he pushes through to finish with only minutes to spare, greeted at the summit by an emotional John. At Halloween, Tommy and John go pumpkin picking with Bambi, things are back on track with Molly, and the house renovation is almost completed. He reflects on where he was last autumn and everything he’s achieved over the past year, and looks forward to a brighter future.

programme.title: Hunting the Rolex Rippers
programme.desc: More and more luxury watches are being snatched off UK streets. In 2022, there was an estimated 60 per cent increase in watch thefts worldwide. It is now the crime of choice for many criminals, seen as easier and more lucrative than drug dealing. In this documentary, journalist Tir Dhondy gets access, for the first time ever, to the gang members behind the crime. She meets the teenage moped riders snatching watches off the street, as well as a gang leader who runs a team of teenage watch rippers and female watch spotters. Tir also comes face-to-face with the 16-year-old who used a machete to steal singer Aled Jones’s £17,000 Rolex in broad daylight.

programme.desc: Single, penniless poet Ruby has recently moved back home to live with her mum, Jen. When their strict Presbyterian neighbours descend on the home for her spoiled sister Eliza's engagement party, Ruby’s only job is to not shame the family...

programme.title: Louis Theroux
programme.desc: Louis Theroux looks back at his earliest documentaries and explores how some people’s most fervent beliefs can bring them into conflict with mainstream society.

programme.title: Louis Theroux
programme.desc: Louis explores how America has managed to take our darkest desires, commodify them and turn them into a saleable product. From his memorable Weird Weekends episodes on porn and rap to films about Las Vegas and the US opioid crisis, this episode explores a very human tendency to jump to the dark side when seeking out pleasure – whether through indulgence, risk-taking or the joy of doing something seen as ‘bad’ or 'wrong’. Louis re-connects with porn-star JJ, who over 20 years ago was just making his way in the adult industry but has since turned his back on that world in favour of a new life in eastern Europe. And Louis catches up once more with Katilia from Heroin Town, whom he last saw hopelessly addicted to drugs, with little sign of turning her life around.

programme.title: Teen Predator/Online Killer
programme.desc: Twenty-year-old Alexander McCartney, already known to police, is arrested and his devices seized after a 12-year-old girl in Scotland reports a serious catfishing abuse incident online. McCartney gives a ‘no comment’ interview while in custody, and without enough physical evidence to charge him, he is released on bail. Back home at his parents’ house, McCartney’s bail conditions are supposed to prevent him from using devices that can connect to the internet. Meanwhile, a second report comes in to the police about another catfishing abuse victim linked to online activity from McCartney’s home address. This time, it involves a young girl in New Zealand. As the police continue to gather up enough physical evidence to charge McCartney, the Cyber Crime Centre completes the analysis of one of his devices, revealing a prolific online predator at a scale never before seen by police in Northern Ireland.

programme.title: Teen Predator/Online Killer
programme.desc: With hundreds of thousands of images of child abuse discovered on McCartney’s devices, the race is on to get him remanded into custody. McCartney is rearrested in the early hours of the morning, at which time police discover McCartney’s phone on his bedside table, where his final victim was abused on Snapchat just hours before. The US Department of Homeland Security notify the police in Northern Ireland of two more catfishing victims, this time in the United States, and a multiagency international investigation is triggered. As McCartney is remanded into custody, police across the world work together to identify and safeguard the thousands of victims discovered on McCartney’s devices. Police are especially keen to identify and locate a 14-year-old girl in Oregon, whose images McCartney used to catfish hundreds of other children. With McCartney due in court to plead guilty to charges of making indecent of images of children and blackmail, the case takes a different turn when Homeland Security finds an obituary page for Cimarron Thomas, one of his victims in West Virginia.

programme.title: The Elon Musk Show
programme.desc: Another look at one of the world’s most polarising billionaires as he swaps rockets and electric cars for raw political power. The programme covers Musk’s tumultuous takeover of Twitter/X, the seismic fallouts of his personal life, and his evolution into a political force on both sides of the Atlantic. With immersive archive footage and revealing testimony from childhood friends, political insiders and former employees, this documentary charts how his quest to 'save humanity' collides with culture wars, AI breakthroughs and far-right movements in the US and UK.

programme.title: Lifeline
programme.desc: Ben Fogle presents an appeal on behalf of Hearing Dogs for Deaf People, a charity that provides support as well as trained assistance dogs to help those living with deafness or hearing loss in the UK.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Melissa, Matt, Becky and Nick – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael boards the Eurostar at London’s St Pancras International, bound for the Belgian capital, Brussels. In the city centre’s sumptuous Theatre Royal, he learns how an impassioned opera performance led to revolution on the streets and the birth of an independent nation. Travelling by tram to the residential district of Saint Gilles, Michael discovers the Belgian origins of art nouveau at the elegant house of architect Victor Horta. Finishing his first day at the headquarters of Nato, opened in 1967, he recalls his time as defence secretary and enjoys a private viewing of its impressive archive.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Yorkshire, farmers and police join forces to tackle a cruel countryside crime. When a tip-off from Farm Watch member James Hinchcliffe sparks a chase across open fields, rural crime officer Sam Blakebrough leads the pursuit of men accused of setting dogs on hares for sport. As officers close in, they’re determined to bring the offenders to justice to send a clear message that such brutality has no place in the countryside. In north Wales, a dairy farmer’s harvest goes up in flames when a devastating case of spontaneous combustion destroys thousands of pounds worth of animal feed. With fires costing UK farms millions every year, experts reveal how this deadly phenomenon ignites silently, and the steps farmers can take to prevent their farmyards against it. And in Cheshire, reporter Paul Colgan trains with a specialist fire and rescue team to learn how they save large farm animals in life-or-death situations.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The freedivers take on the scubas in a race to find a precious lost tankard for a heartbroken son. Detectives Mui and Sam work together to try to solve the mystery of a drone found in Ullswater. Can they find its owner? And over 1,000 bottles dredged from the lakes and fells – scuba Darren shows off his incredible collection.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The unique quiz show where if a player gives an Impossible answer, they are immediately eliminated. Which of the 24 contestants will face the £10,000 question today?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Four more contenders take to the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock to answer questions on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. Clive Myrie asks questions on the films of Judy Garland, The Cure, Hi-de-Hi! and the French Wars of Religion.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: As preparations for the showcase continue, Tippy, Gus and Daisy all attempt to put Louis back on track following the break-up of his marriage. Nic and Vic look to a spiritual ritual to help with their dreams of a child, but Daisy’s forgetfulness may derail the whole thing. Louis’s attempt to pull himself together fails, and a night at the pub has embarrassing consequences. Daisy is overjoyed when Griffin visits but warns him against initiating a casual relationship with a besotted Gus. When that backfires, Griffin decides to leave abruptly, but not before exchanging regrettable words with Daisy, leaving their once-close friendship on the rocks.

programme.title: Sicily: The Wonder of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Historian Michael Scott continues his journey through Sicily, tracing the island's story through the arrival of the Muslim Arabs and then the Normans - times in which religious and cultural tolerance was the order of the day. Michael explores the dark days of the Spanish Inquisition and then delves into the modern world - the unification with Italy and the rise of the Mafia. Today, Sicily faces a new challenge. The island is on the frontline of Europe's migrant crisis but the Sicilian response, formed in part by their own turbulent history, may well surprise many northern Europeans.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination at Warwick Castle. Among the finds are valuable cigarette cards, ancient Peruvian figures, working drawings from a celebrated furniture maker and a vase with a knockout price.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today Flog It! comes from the Blickling estate in north Norfolk. Five antiques experts are on hand to find a selection of objects to take to auction. David Harper is excited by a Rolex oyster watch, and Paul Martin learns more about Lord Lothian, who inherited Blickling in 1930 and played a key role in getting America involved in the Second World War.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Cheryl Baker, Chris Bavin, Axel Blake and Sophie Willan take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Belgian rail journey continues in the Dutch speaking region of Flanders. In Antwerp, he discovers the city's historic multibillion-pound diamond industry and drops in at the workshop of an expert. Just outside the city, Michael boards the Dendermonde to Puurs Heritage Railway, run by volunteers, and gets a chance to drive one of its 1950s diesel engines. Heading to Belgium’s third city, Ghent, Michael visits the magnificent cathedral and marvels at a 15th-century Van Eyck masterpiece, the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, the most stolen painting in the world.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: Marcus wants to impress the locals with a French version of the classic Sunday roast - but first, he needs the perfect poulet. He also gives a masterclass on how to portion a whole chicken and tries to find the best wine to accompany the dish. Later, Marcus finds out how the French enjoy their take on the sandwich. Baguette in hand, he hits the market stalls looking for inspiration.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan continue to celebrate the season at National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland. With a medley of habitats to explore, the show takes to the waterways, home to a multitude of species that reveal a hidden world playing out in the reed beds. Plus a showcase of the wildlife stories playing out across the British Isles. Iolo Williams continues to broadcast live from the Knepp Estate and reveals some its most secretive animals. He also meets the people passionate about rewilding this wildlife haven.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Sandi Toksvig looks at sugar and spice and all things nice with Alice Levine, Jason Manford, Rose Matafeo and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: The magnificent Darren Harriott introduces Jessica Fostekew and Stephen Bailey to the famous Apollo stage.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: The Elon Musk Show
programme.desc: Another look at one of the world’s most polarising billionaires as he swaps rockets and electric cars for raw political power. With immersive archive footage and revealing testimony from childhood friends, political insiders and former employees, this documentary charts how his quest to 'save humanity' collides with culture wars, AI breakthroughs and far-right movements in the US and UK.

programme.title: Iolo's River Valleys
programme.desc: Iolo explores the Teifi river valley and finds a slow worm hunting, meets a coracle fisherman, is thrilled by a fishing otter and watches a pair of kestrels at their nest.

programme.title: This Is a Bomb: The Nevada Casino Heist
programme.desc: When the bomb detonates inside Harvey’s Wagon Wheel Casino, it leaves behind more than shattered concrete and twisted steel. There's a maze of unanswered questions, until a lucky break leads to a psychological stand-off. Calculated risks unravel, loyalties facture, and the truth proves far more complicated than anyone imagined.

David Harper is excited by a Rolex oyster watch, and Paul Martin learns more about Lord Lothian, who inherited Blickling in 1930 and played a key role in getting America involved in the Second World War.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Cheryl Baker, Chris Bavin, Axel Blake and Sophie Willan take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Belgian rail journey continues in the Dutch speaking region of Flanders. In Antwerp, he discovers the city's historic multibillion-pound diamond industry and drops in at the workshop of an expert. Just outside the city, Michael boards the Dendermonde to Puurs Heritage Railway, run by volunteers, and gets a chance to drive one of its 1950s diesel engines. Heading to Belgium’s third city, Ghent, Michael visits the magnificent cathedral and marvels at a 15th-century Van Eyck masterpiece, the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, the most stolen painting in the world.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: Marcus wants to impress the locals with a French version of the classic Sunday roast - but first, he needs the perfect poulet. He also gives a masterclass on how to portion a whole chicken and tries to find the best wine to accompany the dish. Later, Marcus finds out how the French enjoy their take on the sandwich. Baguette in hand, he hits the market stalls looking for inspiration.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan continue to celebrate the season at National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland. With a medley of habitats to explore, the show takes to the waterways, home to a multitude of species that reveal a hidden world playing out in the reed beds. Plus a showcase of the wildlife stories playing out across the British Isles. Iolo Williams continues to broadcast live from the Knepp Estate and reveals some its most secretive animals. He also meets the people passionate about rewilding this wildlife haven.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Sandi Toksvig looks at sugar and spice and all things nice with Alice Levine, Jason Manford, Rose Matafeo and Alan Davies.

programme.title: Live at the Apollo
programme.desc: The magnificent Darren Harriott introduces Jessica Fostekew and Stephen Bailey to the famous Apollo stage.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the news stories of the day. With Victoria Derbyshire.

programme.title: The Elon Musk Show
programme.desc: Another look at one of the world’s most polarising billionaires as he swaps rockets and electric cars for raw political power. The programme covers Musk’s tumultuous takeover of Twitter/X, the seismic fallouts of his personal life, and his evolution into a political force on both sides of the Atlantic. With immersive archive footage and revealing testimony from childhood friends, political insiders and former employees, this documentary charts how his quest to 'save humanity' collides with culture wars, AI breakthroughs and far-right movements in the US and UK.

programme.title: Iolo's River Valleys
programme.desc: Iolo explores the Teifi river valley and finds a slow worm hunting, meets a coracle fisherman, is thrilled by a fishing otter and watches a pair of kestrels at their nest.

programme.title: This Is a Bomb: The Nevada Casino Heist
programme.desc: When the bomb detonates inside Harvey’s Wagon Wheel Casino, it leaves behind more than shattered concrete and twisted steel. There's a maze of unanswered questions, until a lucky break leads to a psychological stand-off. Calculated risks unravel, loyalties facture, and the truth proves far more complicated than anyone imagined.

programme.title: The Elon Musk Show
programme.desc: Another look at one of the world’s most polarising billionaires as he swaps rockets and electric cars for raw political power. The programme covers Musk’s tumultuous takeover of Twitter/X, the seismic fallouts of his personal life, and his evolution into a political force on both sides of the Atlantic. With immersive archive footage and revealing testimony from childhood friends, political insiders and former employees, this documentary charts how his quest to 'save humanity' collides with culture wars, AI breakthroughs and far-right movements in the US and UK.

programme.title: Lifeline
programme.desc: Ben Fogle presents an appeal on behalf of Hearing Dogs for Deaf People, a charity that provides support as well as trained assistance dogs to help those living with deafness or hearing loss in the UK.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Melissa, Matt, Becky and Nick – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael boards the Eurostar at London’s St Pancras International, bound for the Belgian capital, Brussels. In the city centre’s sumptuous Theatre Royal, he learns how an impassioned opera performance led to revolution on the streets and the birth of an independent nation. Travelling by tram to the residential district of Saint Gilles, Michael discovers the Belgian origins of art nouveau at the elegant house of architect Victor Horta. Finishing his first day at the headquarters of Nato, opened in 1967, he recalls his time as defence secretary and enjoys a private viewing of its impressive archive.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Yorkshire, farmers and police join forces to tackle a cruel countryside crime. When a tip-off from Farm Watch member James Hinchcliffe sparks a chase across open fields, rural crime officer Sam Blakebrough leads the pursuit of men accused of setting dogs on hares for sport. As officers close in, they’re determined to bring the offenders to justice to send a clear message that such brutality has no place in the countryside. In north Wales, a dairy farmer’s harvest goes up in flames when a devastating case of spontaneous combustion destroys thousands of pounds worth of animal feed. With fires costing UK farms millions every year, experts reveal how this deadly phenomenon ignites silently, and the steps farmers can take to prevent their farmyards against it. And in Cheshire, reporter Paul Colgan trains with a specialist fire and rescue team to learn how they save large farm animals in life-or-death situations.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The freedivers take on the scubas in a race to find a precious lost tankard for a heartbroken son. Detectives Mui and Sam work together to try to solve the mystery of a drone found in Ullswater. Can they find its owner? And over 1,000 bottles dredged from the lakes and fells – scuba Darren shows off his incredible collection.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The unique quiz show where if a player gives an Impossible answer, they are immediately eliminated. Which of the 24 contestants will face the £10,000 question today?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Four more contenders take to the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock to answer questions on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. Clive Myrie asks questions on the films of Judy Garland, The Cure, Hi-de-Hi! and the French Wars of Religion.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: As preparations for the showcase continue, Tippy, Gus and Daisy all attempt to put Louis back on track following the break-up of his marriage. Nic and Vic look to a spiritual ritual to help with their dreams of a child, but Daisy’s forgetfulness may derail the whole thing. Louis’s attempt to pull himself together fails, and a night at the pub has embarrassing consequences. Daisy is overjoyed when Griffin visits but warns him against initiating a casual relationship with a besotted Gus. When that backfires, Griffin decides to leave abruptly, but not before exchanging regrettable words with Daisy, leaving their once-close friendship on the rocks.

programme.title: Sicily: The Wonder of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Historian Michael Scott continues his journey through Sicily, tracing the island's story through the arrival of the Muslim Arabs and then the Normans - times in which religious and cultural tolerance was the order of the day. Michael explores the dark days of the Spanish Inquisition and then delves into the modern world - the unification with Italy and the rise of the Mafia. Today, Sicily faces a new challenge. The island is on the frontline of Europe's migrant crisis but the Sicilian response, formed in part by their own turbulent history, may well surprise many northern Europeans.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination at Warwick Castle. Among the finds are valuable cigarette cards, ancient Peruvian figures, working drawings from a celebrated furniture maker and a vase with a knockout price.

programme.title: If Walls Could Talk
programme.desc: Friends, families and neighbours come together to reminisce about the special times they’ve shared in this building over the years and how it has shaped much of their lives, creating memories that they cherish. The stage in the Patrician Hall has been host to many performances, from musicians like Sandie Shaw and Roy Orbison to Hollywood actors Stephen Rea and Liam Neeson. The annual Mid-Ulster Drama Festival continues to bring crowds from across Northern Ireland to the hall in Main Street, Carrickmore.

programme.title: Carl Frampton - On Probation
programme.desc: Carl is back with probation officer Toni, who finds out one of her service users is about to become a father again. He is on probation for serious assault and has an historic conviction for assault on a former partner. Carl follows the story as Toni puts measures into place to safeguard the progress the service user has made. But his past conviction catches up with him and threatens to derail him if he doesn’t make serious changes. Meanwhile in Belfast, Carl meets a woman who successfully completed probation and has big plans for her future, but her struggles with alcohol continue to hang over her.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Cheryl Baker, Chris Bavin, Axel Blake and Sophie Willan take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo’s Belgian rail journey continues in the Dutch speaking region of Flanders. In Antwerp, he discovers the city's historic multibillion-pound diamond industry and drops in at the workshop of an expert. Just outside the city, Michael boards the Dendermonde to Puurs Heritage Railway, run by volunteers, and gets a chance to drive one of its 1950s diesel engines. Heading to Belgium’s third city, Ghent, Michael visits the magnificent cathedral and marvels at a 15th-century Van Eyck masterpiece, the Adoration of the Mystic Lamb, the most stolen painting in the world.

programme.title: Marcus Wareing Simply Provence
programme.desc: Marcus wants to impress the locals with a French version of the classic Sunday roast - but first, he needs the perfect poulet. He also gives a masterclass on how to portion a whole chicken and tries to find the best wine to accompany the dish. Later, Marcus finds out how the French enjoy their take on the sandwich. Baguette in hand, he hits the market stalls looking for inspiration.

programme.title: Springwatch
programme.desc: Chris Packham and Michaela Strachan continue to celebrate the season at National Trust Crom in Northern Ireland. He also meets the people passionate about rewilding this wildlife haven.

programme.title: The Elon Musk Show
programme.desc: Another look at one of the world’s most polarising billionaires as he swaps rockets and electric cars for raw political power. The programme covers Musk’s tumultuous takeover of Twitter/X, the seismic fallouts of his personal life, and his evolution into a political force on both sides of the Atlantic. With immersive archive footage and revealing testimony from childhood friends, political insiders and former employees, this documentary charts how his quest to 'save humanity' collides with culture wars, AI breakthroughs and far-right movements in the US and UK.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, family members Melissa, Matt, Becky and Nick – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge, they just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael boards the Eurostar at London’s St Pancras International, bound for the Belgian capital, Brussels. In the city centre’s sumptuous Theatre Royal, he learns how an impassioned opera performance led to revolution on the streets and the birth of an independent nation. Travelling by tram to the residential district of Saint Gilles, Michael discovers the Belgian origins of art nouveau at the elegant house of architect Victor Horta. Finishing his first day at the headquarters of Nato, opened in 1967, he recalls his time as defence secretary and enjoys a private viewing of its impressive archive.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Yorkshire, farmers and police join forces to tackle a cruel countryside crime. When a tip-off from Farm Watch member James Hinchcliffe sparks a chase across open fields, rural crime officer Sam Blakebrough leads the pursuit of men accused of setting dogs on hares for sport. As officers close in, they’re determined to bring the offenders to justice to send a clear message that such brutality has no place in the countryside. In north Wales, a dairy farmer’s harvest goes up in flames when a devastating case of spontaneous combustion destroys thousands of pounds worth of animal feed. With fires costing UK farms millions every year, experts reveal how this deadly phenomenon ignites silently, and the steps farmers can take to prevent their farmyards against it. And in Cheshire, reporter Paul Colgan trains with a specialist fire and rescue team to learn how they save large farm animals in life-or-death situations.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The freedivers take on the scubas in a race to find a precious lost tankard for a heartbroken son. Detectives Mui and Sam work together to try to solve the mystery of a drone found in Ullswater. Can they find its owner? And over 1,000 bottles dredged from the lakes and fells – scuba Darren shows off his incredible collection.

programme.title: Impossible

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Four more contenders take to the black chair under the spotlight and the ticking clock to answer questions on their specialist subjects and general knowledge. Clive Myrie asks questions on the films of Judy Garland, The Cure, Hi-de-Hi! and the French Wars of Religion.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: As preparations for the showcase continue, Tippy, Gus and Daisy all attempt to put Louis back on track following the break-up of his marriage. Nic and Vic look to a spiritual ritual to help with their dreams of a child, but Daisy’s forgetfulness may derail the whole thing. Louis’s attempt to pull himself together fails, and a night at the pub has embarrassing consequences. Daisy is overjoyed when Griffin visits but warns him against initiating a casual relationship with a besotted Gus. When that backfires, Griffin decides to leave abruptly, but not before exchanging regrettable words with Daisy, leaving their once-close friendship on the rocks.

programme.title: Sicily: The Wonder of the Mediterranean
programme.desc: Historian Michael Scott continues his journey through Sicily, tracing the island's story through the arrival of the Muslim Arabs and then the Normans - times in which religious and cultural tolerance was the order of the day. Michael explores the dark days of the Spanish Inquisition and then delves into the modern world - the unification with Italy and the rise of the Mafia. Today, Sicily faces a new challenge. The island is on the frontline of Europe's migrant crisis but the Sicilian response, formed in part by their own turbulent history, may well surprise many northern Europeans.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel presents the show in which members of the public are invited to bring along their antiques for examination at Warwick Castle. Among the finds are valuable cigarette cards, ancient Peruvian figures, working drawings from a celebrated furniture maker and a vase with a knockout price.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘teddy’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We see lots of different teddies – a big teddy, some small teddies, a rainbow teddy and some cuddly teddies. There’s a fluffy teddy, a flower teddy and even a flying teddy. We also get to meet Dee’s special teddy.

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch
programme.desc: Lu and Declan race their home toys, and Declan is a bit careless.

programme.title: Kiri and Lou
programme.desc: Kiri, Lou and Sorry are playing tickle monster. They are very surprised when the grumpy Ichtheo wants to join in, but he turns out to be the best monster of all.

programme.title: Froglets
programme.desc: On Alex's birthday, the Froglets lift off in a hot-air balloon for a high-flying party.

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a park, where they watch a girl on rollerskates with her dad. She takes off the skates but accidentally kicks one so that it rolls away down a hill. The girl and her father take off in pursuit of the runaway skate, leaving the other one. Toodloo jumps on it and rolls away down the hill. The other Twirlywoos follow Toodloo down paths and steps and skate ramps until the skate comes to rest on top of a slide in a playground. Toodloo's enthusiastic waving to the others (who are at the bottom of the slide) causes the skate to tip and hurtle down the slide. Toodloo crashes into the other Twirlywoos, and the skate continues on its journey, only to be reunited with the girl and her dad! The Twirlywoos return to the boat to discover the Twirlywoo Screen. A series of sloping lines appear, followed by a marble. When Toodloo reaches up and touches the marble, it starts to roll down the course until it drops onto the floor of the boat. More and more marbles draw on and roll down until the wall is full of rolling marbles which all fall down and roll away into Peekaboo's house.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Maddie meets Alfie and Harley at the park to play some games relating to different parts of the body. Mr Tumble and the toys make up a dance routine. Everyone gets moving and grooving in the spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words foot, hand and dancing.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Preschool series. It's time to wake up, but Tinky Winky isn't feeling well. Soon after, Tinky Winky feels better, but now Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po don't feel well.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies Tobias, Inam, Isaac, Enya, Hawa, Jean and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities, too! Inside everyone’s bags are shakers and rattles which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate shaker or rattle inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The fun song ‘Dingle Dangle Scarecrow’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Together Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children share a teddy bears’ picnic with pretend buns and tea, learning British Sign Language signs for ship, soldier and jump, then sing and sign When I Was One.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: It’s a busy day down in the garden, as Aaron, Adrian and Nelly are looking for minibeasts! Their journey starts when they lift some logs and stones to see what’s underneath, uncovering a family of woodlice scuttling around. But where are they going, and what’s the rush? Right on cue, Chatterpot’s ready with a clever clue to help Aaron and the buds find the answer.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Murphi is in the middle of a mega clean-up in the attic, but he can't find Rebecca’s lost hat. His magic cleaning machine goes wrong and causes mayhem, which gives him a monster make idea - a paper banana skin! The Mini Monsters create wonderful scrap bag monsters, while Rebecca’s grandpa tries to create a new ice cream flavour and a dreamy creamy sundae. The Recycling Express brings an old box with a window, which Murphi and Rebecca transform into a terrific box truck.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: When Ginger gets stung by an Appleflyus, it leaves a painful and incredibly itchy sore.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey can't wait to get to the monkey bars as Dad takes her and Bingo on a wagon ride to the park. But her patience is tested when Dad keeps stopping to chat with other grown-ups.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: After hearing a strange sound, the Squirrels turn to Duggee to help identify its source. They learn about sound waves, and that you can listen for different qualities in the sounds, such as if it’s loud, quiet, high or low. Describing the sound can help you work out where it’s coming from, so Duggee lets the Squirrels close their eyes as they listen to sounds and make their guesses.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Howdy diddly diddly do! This song is about all the different things we learn with Duggee to earn our badges. From singing to painting, dancing, playing, and making friends too!

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk to the beach to make funny faces in the sand. Along the way, they count the boats in the harbour, see a heron take off, spot a boat that looks like a whale and find a tiny crab in the rockpool.

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: Henry and his little sister Sophie make crowns and become King Henry and Queen Sophie. Along with their noble knights (Mummy and Mama!), they head to the local park on a royal quest to rescue their toy turtle Pebbles, who is trapped in a castle! Back home, the royals relax with a rainbow waterfall and water squirters. It’s not long before Henry and the whole family are soaking wet!

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Nyama is a type of stew from Zimbabwe. It uses a special type of young cabbage leaf called spring greens, which Pippa adds to her stew along with lots of other delicious ingredients. Pippa works hard preparing all the spices, chicken, tomatoes and shallots to make her tasty nyama for her friends. Pippa’s table is animal themed, complete with zebra prints and a toy giraffe! With her mum’s help, Pippa serves the nyama with sadza, a type of dumpling from Zimbabwe, and encourages her friends to eat with their fingers, as is traditional.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: Maddie is finding out about repeating patterns. She visits a butterfly sanctuary to learn how the life cycle of a butterfly works. Maddie uses her special microscope camera to show us the marvellous moment when a tiny caterpillar hatches out of its egg, and we see three Owl butterflies emerge from their pupa and spread their wings for the first time. Then Maddie heads to a wallpaper factory to learn how a repeat pattern is designed and the different colours are printed. She uses her special cameras to see how a printing machine uses rollers to print each separate colour and make the whole pattern repeat.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Disability assistance dog Tinks visits Clip-Clop Stables with Charli, where they meet a very tall horse called Mist, who is taking Charli for her first ever horse-riding lesson.

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet a vulture called Ethel. Vultures have amazing eyesight and can spot food from high up in the sky. To meet their next animal, Aneeshwar and Lizzie must go far down below. The brittlestar lives underwater in the ocean. This incredible creature has five long arms and a body called a disc. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Gramps teaches Waffle to read and stages a garden performance to showcase Waffle’s new talent. Jelly digs under the fence to join in, causing a surprise entrance from Mrs Hobbs.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona and Baba help a little lamb to find her mum.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: When Toad finds himself with a case of puddle hiccups, it’s up to Yukee and the rest of the garden gang to find a cure.

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Mum and Dad are heading out for the evening, and Mum has already told their babysitter, Uncle George, not to turn the house upside down! Surely there are ways to have the best night ever without making a big mess…

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are having fun playing games but are surprised to find out that Betty didn’t always enjoy playing. Since her first day at Squirrel Club, she always impressed everyone with her confidence and independence, but at first she didn’t know how to join in with the others. Luckily, Duggee had a great idea to bring all the Squirrels together.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Children's animation. Five and friends discover a hole that makes their heads fall off! Learn how to count up and down and how to add to five with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: The adventures of 26 lively letters who can make words come to life by holding hands. From A to Z, every Alphablock has fun discovering the magic of wordplay. When the Alphablocks can't decide between rock and pop, it's time for a battle of the bands to see which is best.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Mr Tumble gets in a muddle while helping Grandad Tumble look after the garden. Justin meets Ryan, his new friend, in a walled garden to help take care of the plants. George joins them to do some watering. There's a decorative recycling spotty surprise. Featuring signs for the words seeds, garden and plant.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies bounce on the Tubby Bouncy. Po bounces as high as a cloud, then Laa-Laa bounces higher, Dipsy bounces even higher and Tinky Winky bounces highest of all.

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how shells play an important role in the environment. They find out that shells help protect the creatures that live inside them and that many animals grow their own shells, which get bigger as they grow. On the way, they look for snails in the park and find lots of different shells on the beach and in rock pools.

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: When a rogue ball destroys Mr Parks’s competition-ready bug hotel, Evie, Taran and Jaz help him rebuild it using a combination of football skills and teamwork.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this episode, Grace shows off three amazing machines that are all like animals. Grace goes for a ride in a vehicle like a shark, shows off a machine that flies by flapping its wings like a bird and then goes for a drive in a big robot insect.

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: It's the first day of Pup School. Dodge overcomes his first day nerves as he meets lots of new friends. The pups settle into their class activities with their new teacher Miss Collie.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger joins the baby Pea-Rexes on their expedition to find dinner.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: Paani saves a newborn goose, then seeks the Octonauts' help to decipher its behaviour.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Peter Rabbit wants to grow up to be just like his late father - he has big paws to fill. But with his father's journal and the help of his best friends Benjamin and Lily, Peter is ready for some fun and delightful new discoveries. Benjamin gets a pet snail, but his friends can't see the appeal, especially when it attracts the attention of Old Brown!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels meet a Scrufflelump in the woods, and despite Duggee’s reservations, take him in. But they soon learn the responsibilities of taking care of a pet.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Vida and friends move a piano all the way across Sweetwood to save Pippen’s concert!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Supertato is delighted when Evil Pea comes to his birthday party, but Carrot is suspicious. Soon Evil Pea unleashes the Mini Peas, who try to steal Supertato’s birthday present.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: Weasy promises to go camping with the ducklings, but he wants to watch football instead. During half-time, Weasy attempts to finish camping as quickly as possible.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Ted the bus wants to be faster, and Mojo swops every top to try to make it happen. But it’s Bo’s homemade rocket that gives Ted the boost he needs... all the way into space!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo teach Unicorse good manners, so he can ask Mum out on a date.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: The Heelers take a long riverside walk, but Bingo’s legs are tired and she wants a piggyback. To distract her, Mum and Dad invent fun games and get her little legs moving again!

programme.title: Zog
programme.desc: The fearsome Great Gnanna Gnome has a case of bottom-fungal-itis. Zog and the doctors must figure out how to treat the mushroom without incurring Gnanna's anger.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: Penny brings a dinosaur fossil to the nursery, while Bonnie and Hamish plan a secret dino dance. And mysterious footprints have Penny wondering if there’s a real dino on the island.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: The Brooklyn-Bells are on holiday with Gramps, so Waffle is staying at Angela’s dog kennels for a couple of nights. During a face-to-face call with Waffle, the Brooklyn-Bells check their wonder dog is settling in and ensure he has his favourite snuggly toy with him, PegStar. Angela tries to settle Waffle but he whines, he’s missing his Brooklyn-Bell family and looks at their photo on the wall of his kennel. Angela resorts to calling the Brooklyn-Bells and explains that when dogs are very disruptive, she expects their owners, or someone they know, to pick them up. Jess has an idea – there’s someone who might be able to pick Waffle up in the morning - Mrs Hobbs!

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Finn puts on a magic show at the bakery and wants to do it all by himself. It goes well - until he gets stuck. Rafi secretly makes a wish, and suddenly his hat is full of bunnies! The crowd laughs, but Finn is upset that the show isn’t his anymore. With Ruby’s help, they use carrot cake to guide the bunnies back into the hat. When the wish ends, Finn finishes the show on his own. He proves he can shine, and Rafi realises that friends sometimes need space to do things their own way.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo, Gran Gran and Cynthia build a bug hotel in Cynthia’s garden and welcome some new residents. JoJo learns that different insects are attracted to different materials and environments in the bug hotel. Ladybirds like straw, beetles like dry leaves and bees like nooks and crannies. Gran Gran gives JoJo her own mini bug hotel for the insects in her own garden.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Inspired by a nature documentary, Sarah and Duck attempt to take photographs of birds.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: A meteor shower is about to hit the Clangers' planet. Major and Small shelter on the Iron Chicken's nest, while the others find cover in the living cave. But when the shower stops, they find that a giant meteor has fallen and blocked the double doors to the inside. With Major and Small not yet back, Mother, Granny and Tiny have to think of a way to remove the boulder themselves. They make their way to Major's workshop to see if they can invent a machine to help.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa play tickle chase with a Tweetie feather. At Play Time, they choose to play with a feather duster, aka a tickle wand! MeMo chases BaBa with the wand. It is fun at first, but then BaBa wants to stop playing.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures. The Pontipines and the Wottingers are out for a walk in the garden. Mrs Pontipine spots something through her binoculars - it is the Ninky Nonk! Makka Pakka, Upsy Daisy and Igglepiggle all join the Pontipines and Wottingers for a ride on the Ninky Nonk.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Andy Day invites you to join the CBeebies House Club for a welcoming Bedtime Story.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s Cauliflower creaking away as she grows and sings her catchy Cauliflower Creak song.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Coco discovers Bing's dressing-up box so they both dress up. Coco is Princess Cococapono and Bing is, of course, King Bing. But there is only one crown and both need it to complete their outfits. When the crown gets broken, Flop helps them to make new crowns out of the broken pieces.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: It's a windy day in Teletubbyland and Dipsy's hat blows away. Po helps Dipsy get the hat back, while in Tummy Tales, children have fun playing on a windy beach.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Preschool animation. Mo is always there to help, but Tee is getting bigger and wants to do everything by himself.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: All the fruit and veggies in the supermarket are enjoying Fruit and Veggie Friends Day, but Evil Pea is determined to ruin it. After Supertato inadvertently stops her from taking the friendship cards and launching attacks with her pea shooter and freezy hose, Evil Pea tries to cover the party in ice cream. But when her plan goes wrong, she's rolled away on the ice cream tub, and Supertato saves her. Supertato has been trying to give her a friendship card all day long - Evil Pea furiously accepts it!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing has broken his arm and is struggling to do his usual activities. Petting Arlo hurts, playing with blocks hurts, and even drinking juice hurts. But when Bing and Sula draw together it doesn't hurt, and so he forgets about his arm and does a big, painful 'hoppity voosh'! Amma gently explains to Bing, Sula and Flop that when she broke her arm, she learnt that sometimes you have to ask for help.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Bo is tired and falls asleep in the middle of hunting for Fabio’s lost inflatable fruit. It’s up to Mojo to finish the job - without waking up poor, exhausted Bo!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: At Squirrel Club, Duggee forgets how to woof, Duggly comes to visit, Roly celebrates Potato Time, and Billy teaches everyone the Bugatron dance!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels notice that Happy looks and seems different – he is frowning, his smile is upside down, and he’s wearing new trainers! When they check in on him, Happy is frustrated, but he can’t seem to identify where his frustration is coming from. They turn to Duggee for help, who uses his feeling cards to explain an array of feelings to Happy. All the Squirrels help by relaying their past experiences and the feelings that they evoked.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo teach Unicorse good manners, so he can ask Mum out on a date.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: The Heelers take a long riverside walk, but Bingo’s legs are tired and she wants a piggyback. To distract her, Mum and Dad invent fun games and get her little legs moving again!

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Glitch wants to ski, so the Grimbots give Table Mountain a snowy peak, which threatens its rare plants.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When Peter tries to get the last plum from Mr McGregor's tree, he finds that a mysterious thief has beaten him to it!

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. Peso and Kwazii venture down to the midnight zone to help a hurt creature, but what they find is a shipwreck, haunted by a spooky-looking long-armed squid.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Squarey, we're not in Numberland any more! Four visits Flatland, where the flat shapes live, and becomes a real square. Learn about 2D shapes with the Numberblocks.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: It's O's birthday, but R has forgotten to get him a present! Can she magic up a big wheel, a helter-skelter and a hall of mirrors from thin air? This episode introduces the '-er-' digraph, the '-air-', '-ure-' and '-ear-' trigraphs and the words air, fair, chair, pair, cure, big, bigger, thin, thinner, ear, hear, near and box.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: The neighbours have left a 'please take' box outside their house, so Nick picks out some exciting things. The little crochet doll he finds looks a bit sad. Can Norman and the Popcasters help write a song to cheer it up?

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: We sing a calming song about counting frogs with Mrs Weaver.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Lift is in a cheeky mood and makes Bella a snack of one little pea! In the Fortress of Fun, Kingsley and Queenie have fun looking for peas with the Playtimers in their Pea Party game, whilst in the Cloud Kitchen, a pea pod from Foggy reminds Patch of the time he spent at the Veggieville Music Festival. In Boxtropolis, Sketch and the Playtimers make Wiggle Wiggle Caterpillars using bouncy balls!
